newsitem.title: UK: Applied Materials to site training in UK.
newsitem.headline: Applied Materials to site training in UK.

text.p: U.S. semiconductor equipment and technology supplier Applied Materials Inc said on Friday it would set up a European training centre in the north-east of England.
The company said in a statement that its European technical centre would help to plug the skills gap which had threatened to slow the pace of growth in Europe's semiconductor industry.
The announcement is a major boost for the north-east of England, which has already attracted huge semiconductor investment from Germany's Siemens AG and Japan's Fujitsu Ltd of Japan.

A spokesman for the Northern Development Co, which helps to attract investment to the region, said the Applied Materials training centre would provide the cornerstone for a planned 15 million stg European Microelectronics Institute in north Tyneside.
Although Applied Materials did not disclose financial details of its investment, it is believed to total several million pounds.

Rodney Griffiths, president of Applied Materials Europe, said that while the European workforce is highly skilled, "one major resource limitation has been the training and specialized skills necessary to support technology and processes used in semiconductor manufacture."

The training centre will offer six-month courses, mainly to science and engineering graduates. The spokesman said the NDC would be working with universities in the region to try to set up a formal qualification.
